Anything else is treated as paragraph text. """ import html import re _HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.+?)\s*#*\s*$") _ULIST = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*+]\s+(.*)$") _OLIST = re.compile(r"^\s*\d+[.)]\s+(.*)$") _FENCE = re.compile(r"^```\s*([\w+-]*)\s*$") _LINK = re.compile(r"\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)\s]+)\)") _CODE = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`") _STRONG = re.compile(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*") _EM = re.compile(r"\*(.+?)\*|_(.+?)_") _PLACEHOLDER = re.compile(r"\x00(\d+)\x00") def inline(text: str) -> str: out = html.escape(text, quote=False) # Code spans and link targets are swapped for placeholders so the # emphasis rules below cannot touch them. stash: list[str] = [] def hold(fragment: str) -> str: stash.append(fragment) return f"\x00{len(stash) - 1}\x00" out = _CODE.sub(lambda m: hold(f"{m.group(1)}"), out) out = _LINK.sub(lambda m: hold(f'') + m.group(1) + "", out) out = _STRONG.sub(r"\1", out) out = _EM.sub(lambda m: f"{m.group(1) or m.group(2)}", out) return _PLACEHOLDER.sub(lambda m: stash[int(m.group(1))], out) def to_html(source: str) -> str: blocks: list[str] = [] paragraph: list[str] = [] list_tag: str | None = None list_items: list[str] = [] in_fence = False fence_lang = "" fence_lines: list[str] = [] def flush_paragraph() -> None: if paragraph: blocks.append(f"

{inline(' '.join(paragraph))}

") paragraph.clear() def flush_list() -> None: nonlocal list_tag if list_tag: items = "".join(f"
  • {inline(item)}
    • " for item in list_items) blocks.append(f"<{list_tag}>{items}") list_items.clear() list_tag = None def flush_fence() -> None: attr = f' class="language-{fence_lang}"' if fence_lang else "" code = html.escape("\n".join(fence_lines), quote=False) blocks.append(f"
    {code}
    ") fence_lines.clear() for line in source.splitlines(): if in_fence: if line.strip() == "```": flush_fence() in_fence = False else: fence_lines.append(line) continue fence = _FENCE.match(line) if fence: flush_paragraph() flush_list() in_fence = True fence_lang = fence.group(1) continue if not line.strip(): flush_paragraph() flush_list() continue heading = _HEADING.match(line) if heading: flush_paragraph() flush_list() level = len(heading.group(1)) blocks.append(f"{inline(heading.group(2))}") continue for pattern, tag in ((_ULIST, "ul"), (_OLIST, "ol")): item = pattern.match(line) if item: flush_paragraph() if list_tag != tag: flush_list() list_tag = tag list_items.append(item.group(1)) break else: if list_tag and line.startswith((" ", "\t")): list_items[-1] += " " + line.strip() continue flush_list() paragraph.append(line.strip()) if in_fence: flush_fence() flush_paragraph() flush_list() return "\n".join(blocks) + ("\n" if blocks else "")

content.text:
`to_html` is now split into per-block handlers, and nested lists work. All 51 tests pass: the original 43, plus 8 new nested-list tests. I haven't committed anything.

**Step 1: refactor.** `to_html` now delegates to a small `_Parser` class in `quillmark/markdown.py`. Each block type has its own handler: `heading`, `fence_open`/`fence_body`/`flush_fence`, `list_item`/`flush_list`, and `text`/`flush_paragraph`. A `feed` method dispatches each line in the same order as the old loop. The suite stayed green after this step alone, before any nesting.

**Step 2: nested lists.** Each list item now records its depth (one level per two spaces of indent), its tag, and its text. `flush_list` renders them recursively, so a sublist sits inside its parent `<li>`.
- A top-level `ul`/`ol` switch still starts a separate block, as before.
- A deeper indent jump, such as four spaces under a top-level item, is treated as one level deeper.
- An indented first item is treated as top level.
- I updated the module docstring to mention nesting.

Your uncommitted changes to `inline()` and its tests were already in the working tree. I left them in place.

**Behaviour change.** Before, an indented marker like `  - b` was a sibling of the previous item. Now it is a sublist. That is what the feature asks for, but flat output for indented bullets differs from before.
